text.p: A weary Thomas Muster squeezed past Italian qualifier Gianluca Pozzi in a tight 7-5 6-4 first round battle at the $800,000 CA Trophy on Wednesday.
The top seeded Austrian, ranked third in the world, blamed his weak display on fatigue following a recent bout of flu which also led to the 29-year-old losing in the first round in Lyon last week.
"I have had too many things on my plate lately, a bad cold, the ITF meeting in London, and a tiring promotion tour," he said. "I am not playing at the level I would like to."
Muster's trip to London failed to win a reprieve for the Austrian Davis Cup team following their walkout in Sao Paolo against Brazil last month, and his week is by no means certain to improve.
His next match is against Sweden's Stefan Edberg, an opponent he has met eight times in the past without any success.
"If I want to win against Edberg, I have to play much better than I did today. I simply just have to do everything better.
"He (Edberg) is obviously the favourite here on the hard court. But my goal is simply to win the next match," said Muster, a finalist here in 1988, 1993 and 1995.
The lefthanded Austrian finally secured victory over Pozzi after a little over an hour and a half, converting his third match point with a thundering backhand pass.

In earlier first round matches, Russia's French Open winner and number three seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov eliminated Germany's David Prinosil 7-6 6-2, while Frenchman Arnaud Boetsch sent sixth seeded Chilean Marcelo Rios crashing out 6-2 6-4.
Australian Open champion Boris Becker dropped a set before overcoming Australia's Mark Woodforde 7-6 (7-2) 3-6 6-4 in a little under two hours.
Fifth seed Becker was not unduly troubled by a wrist injury sustained at Wimbledon which caused him to pull out of last week's tournament in Lyon.
"I feel in good shape. I felt no pain in my wrist today and I hope it stays that way tommorrow," he said. "But I was not happy with my volley, obviously my wrist is not completely strong yet."
On Thursday, Becker meets fellow German Michael Stich. The pair last met a year ago at Stuttgart with Stich winning in straight sets.
